questions.stem: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "Today there is a growing awareness that mental well-being needs to be given as much attention as physical health." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
Today there is a growing awareness that mental well-being needs to be given as much attention as physical health. This view deserves our serious attention, especially when modern life keeps us under constant pressure and quiet mental troubles often go unnoticed.

To begin with, ignoring our inner state can cost us dearly. Long-term stress and anxiety lead to sleeplessness and poor concentration, which in turn damage both our bodies and our performance. Take my own experience as an example: before an important exam, I was so anxious that I could not sleep for nights and ended up doing far worse than usual. Only after I talked to my friends and kept a regular routine did my mind settle down and my results recover. This taught me that the mind clearly deserves the same care we give the body.

In conclusion, we should value our minds as much as our bodies. Only when individuals pay attention to their feelings and society offers more support can we truly live a healthy and balanced life.

sections.note: 听力为历年真题原文，题目与答案为官方标准答案；在线音频由语音合成朗读原文，不是考场录音；换浏览器、换手机都能播。

transcript.text: A woman was charged with allegedly violating a Rhode Island city law against feeding wild animals. The 55-year-old woman's neighbors blame her for making the area's rat problem worse.
transcript.zh: 一名女子被指控涉嫌违反罗德岛州某市禁止喂食野生动物的法律。这名55岁女子的邻居指责她加剧了该地区的老鼠问题。

transcript.text: Newly installed cameras captured several rats active in the middle of the day. Neighbors say that it's even worse during the night.
transcript.zh: 新安装的摄像头拍摄到数只老鼠在白天活动。邻居们表示夜间情况更加严重。

transcript.text: The woman and her parents, who own the home, told reporters that she's being charged for feeding birds.
transcript.zh: 这名女子及其拥有该房产的父母告诉记者,她被指控的原因是喂鸟。

transcript.text: "Who would have known just loving animals gets you that much trouble," she said.
transcript.zh: 她说:"谁能想到仅仅是喜爱动物就会惹来这么大的麻烦。"

transcript.text: It is prohibited to feed any wild animals including birds in Rhode Island City. Nevertheless, while the woman's intention was to feed birds, it is clear that rats were also benefiting.
transcript.zh: 在罗德岛市,禁止喂食包括鸟类在内的任何野生动物。然而,尽管该女子的本意是喂鸟,但显然老鼠也从中受益。

transcript.text: Anthony Moretti, director of the city administration, said he saw more than 20 rats near the woman's home. He said it will take months to get the problem under control.
transcript.zh: 市政管理部门主任Anthony Moretti表示,他在该女子家附近看到了20多只老鼠。他说控制这个问题需要数月时间。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the report about the 55-year-old woman?

options.text: She was involved in a conflict with bird lovers.
She was charged with mistreating animals.
She was on bad terms with her neighbors.
She was accused of violating a city law.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：A woman was charged with allegedly violating a Rhode Island city law against feeding wild animals.信号：导语句即答案句 。A woman was charged with allegedly violating a Rhode Island city law against feeding wild animals. …

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：She was involved in a conflict with bird lovers. 利用录音多次提到的 birds / feeding birds 制造「她与爱鸟者起冲突」的假象，但录音通篇只说她「以为自己在喂鸟」，从未出现她和任何 bird lovers 群体的冲突，是典型的「听到 bird 就想选」。 借用原文：was charged with allegedly violating a Rhode Island city law against feeding wild animals
optionAnalysis.B: 偷换概念：She was charged with mistreating animals. 沿用了录音里 was charged with 的句式结构和 animals 这个词，但把违法内容从「违反禁止投喂的市法规」偷换成「虐待动物」——录音从未提及任何虐待行为，反而她声称是「出于爱」在喂。 借用原文：The 55-year-old woman's neighbors blame her
optionAnalysis.C: 过度推断：She was on bad terms with her neighbors. 利用录音 The 55-year-old woman's neighbors blame her 里出现的 neighbors blame 来诱选；但 blame 是针对此次鼠患的具体指责，新闻并未交代他们一贯关系不和，把「具体事件上的指责」升级成「长期关系恶劣」属于过度推断。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（was charged with allegedly violating a Rhode Island city law ↔ was accused of violating a city law charge≈accuse 同义替换）

questions.evidenceText: A woman was charged with allegedly violating a Rhode Island city law against feeding wild animals.

questions.stem: What did the director of the city administration say at the end of the news report?

options.text: It will take time to solve the rat problem.
All wild animals should be well protected.
The woman was not to blame for the situation.
No one should go unpunished for violating law.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P6）：Anthony Moretti, director of the city administration, said he saw more than 20 rats near the woman's home. He said it will take months to get the problem under control.信号：末段官员引语 。He said it will take months to get the problem under control. 出现在新闻最后一段、由 director of the city admin…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：All wild animals should be well protected. 借用了录音里多次出现的 wild animals 做诱饵，但官员从未谈论「应保护所有野生动物」这种价值口号，他只是描述老鼠数量和耗时，All wild animals 属于绝对化范围扩大。 借用原文：Nevertheless, while the woman's intention was to feed birds, it is clear that rats were also benefiting.
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：The woman was not to blame for the situation. 与录音传递的态度相反——录音 Nevertheless, while the woman's intention was to feed birds, it is clear that rats were also benefiting. 明确指出「尽管她本意是喂鸟，但老鼠也因此得利」，是把责任与她挂钩，而非为她开脱。 借用原文：It is prohibited to feed any wild animals including birds in Rhode Island City.
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：No one should go unpunished for violating law. 看似呼应录音里 It is prohibited to feed any wild animals 的法律口吻，但这是新闻叙述者的背景交代，并非「director of the city administration」在末尾说的话，且 No one should go unpunished 这种绝对化执法口号录音中并未出现。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（it will take months to get the problem under control ↔ It will take time to solve the rat problem. months≈time, under control≈solve）

questions.evidenceText: Anthony Moretti, director of the city administration, said he saw more than 20 rats near the woman's home. He said it will take months to get the problem under control.

transcript.text: To prepare for eventually sending astronauts to Mars, NASA began taking applications Friday for four people to live for a year in Mars Dune Alpha. That's a 1,700-square-foot Martian habitat inside a building in Houston.
transcript.zh: 为了准备最终将宇航员送往火星, NASA于周五开始接受四人申请,让他们在Mars Dune Alpha中生活一年。这是位于休斯顿一座建筑内的一个1700平方英尺的火星栖息地。

transcript.text: The paid volunteers will work in an environment similar to Mars. They will have limited communications with family, restricted food and resources.
transcript.zh: 这些有偿志愿者将在类似火星的环境中工作。他们与家人的通讯将受到限制,食物和资源也会受限。

transcript.text: NASA is planning three experiments with the first one starting in the fall next year. Food will all be ready-to-eat space food. Some plants will be grown, but not potatoes like in the movie The Martian.
transcript.zh: NASA正在计划三次实验,第一次实验将于明年秋季开始。食物将全部是即食太空食品。会种植一些植物,但不会像电影《火星救援》中那样种植土豆。

transcript.text: "We want to understand how humans perform in them," said lead scientist Grace Douglas. "We are looking at Mars-realistic situations."
transcript.zh: 首席科学家Grace Douglas说:"我们想了解人类在这些环境中的表现。我们关注的是符合火星实际情况的场景。"

transcript.text: The application process opens Friday and they're not seeking just anybody. The requirements are strict, including a master's degree in a science, engineering or math field or pilot experience. Only American citizens or permanent U.S. residents are acceptable. Applicants must be between 30 and 55 and in good physical health.
transcript.zh: 申请流程于周五开放,他们寻找的并非普通人选。要求非常严格,包括拥有科学、工程或数学领域的硕士学位或飞行员经验。只接受美国公民或美国永久居民。申请人必须年龄在30至55岁之间,身体健康状况良好。

transcript.text: Attitude is key, said former Canadian astronaut Chris Hadfield. He said the participants need to be super competent, resourceful, and not relying on other people to feel comfortable.
transcript.zh: 加拿大前宇航员Chris Hadfield表示,态度是关键。他说参与者需要非常能干、足智多谋,不依赖他人也能感到自在。

questions.stem: What does NASA require the paid volunteers to do?

options.text: Communicate with astronauts in Mars Dune Alpha.
Work in an environment resembling Mars.
Build a Martian habitat in Houston.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：The paid volunteers will work in an environment similar to Mars.信号：题干主语原词复现 。题干主体是 the paid volunteers，录音第 2 段开头 The paid volunteers will work in an environment similar to Mar…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项里出现了录音原词 Mars Dune Alpha，但录音从头到尾没说志愿者要去和宇航员通讯，只在第 2 段提了 They will have limited communications with family——是和家人有限通讯，不是和宇航员通讯。把 Mars Dune Alpha 这个专名扣到一个原文没说的动作上骗你听到原词就选。 借用原文：a 1,700-square-foot Martian habitat inside a building in Houston
optionAnalysis.C: 录音说 a 1,700-square-foot Martian habitat inside a building in Houston，确实有 Martian habitat 和 Houston 两个原词，但志愿者是住进去而不是建。选项 Build a Martian habitat in Houston 把 habitat 和 Houston 拼到 Build 这个动词上，是把建造者的事安到志愿者头上，典型张冠李戴。 借用原文：NASA began taking applications Friday
optionAnalysis.D: 录音第 1 段念了 NASA began taking applications Friday，第 5 段也说 The application process opens Friday——Friday 这个词真的反复出现，但说的是 NASA 周五开始收申请，而不是 NASA 要求志愿者周五前递申请。Friday 是被盗用来骗 听到就想选 的原词。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（will work in an environment similar to Mars ↔ Work in an environment resembling Mars similar to 替换 resembling）

questions.evidenceText: The paid volunteers will work in an environment similar to Mars.

questions.stem: What will the participants in the project eat?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：Food will all be ready-to-eat space food. Some plants will be grown, but not potatoes like in the movie The Martian.信号：Food 起首+all 强调 。录音第 3 段那一句 Food will all be ready-to-eat space food. 以题干关键词 Food 起首，且用 all 这种范围最大、最绝对的修饰词强调全…

optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：录音从头到尾没有出现 organic 这个词，也没说食物是天然有机的；选项 Food that is organic. 是凭电影或常识对火星实验食物的想象，属于录音没说就硬塞的未提及干扰。
optionAnalysis.C: 录音确实念了 Some plants will be grown，grown 这个原词被选项 Food they grow. 直接盗用；但原文用 Some 限定只是一些，且强调 Food will all be ready-to-eat——食物全部是即食的，植物种植只是次要补充，不是吃的来源。听到 grown 就想选 C 是这道题最大的诱惑。 借用原文：but not potatoes like in the movie The Martian
optionAnalysis.D: 录音里 but not potatoes like in the movie The Martian 明确用 but not 否定了土豆，选项 Potatoes mostly. 却把它当作主食呈现，与原文方向完全相反。potatoes 这个原词被盗来诱惑那些被电影《火星救援》带偏的考生。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（ready-to-eat space food ↔ Ready-made food ready-to-eat=ready-made）

questions.evidenceText: Food will all be ready-to-eat space food. Some plants will be grown, but not potatoes like in the movie The Martian.

transcript.text: A Japanese mayor apologized Thursday for biting the Olympic gold medal of a softball player. Nagoya mayor Takashi Kawamura had praised an athlete, Miu Goto, during a public media event. He asked her to put the medal around his neck. Kawamura then bit into it.
transcript.zh: 日本一位市长周四为咬了一名垒球运动员的奥运金牌道歉。名古屋市长河村隆之在一次公开媒体活动中表扬了运动员后藤希友。他请她把奖牌挂在他的脖子上。随后河村咬了那枚奖牌。

transcript.text: Biting a medal in front of journalists and photographers has become a common pose for Olympic medalists. However, it is only for the winners themselves, not others.
transcript.zh: 在记者和摄影师面前咬奖牌已成为奥运奖牌获得者的常见姿势。然而,这只适用于获奖者本人,而非其他人。

transcript.text: "I'm really sorry that I hurt the treasure of the gold medalist," Kawamura told reporters Thursday.
transcript.zh: 河村周四告诉记者:"我真的很抱歉伤害了金牌得主的珍宝。"

transcript.text: The mayor said the medal was undamaged, though he offered to pay for the cost of a new one.
transcript.zh: 市长表示奖牌没有损坏,不过他提出愿意支付一枚新奖牌的费用。

transcript.text: Goto, however, has accepted the International Olympic Committee's offer of a replacement, according to Japanese media reports.
transcript.zh: 然而,据日本媒体报道,后藤已接受国际奥委会提供的替换奖牌。

transcript.text: The scene broadcast on television prompted thousands of complaints to city hall. Some Olympians said they treat their medals as treasures and that it was disrespectful and unacceptable for Kawamura to bite one.
transcript.zh: 电视上播出的这一幕引发了数千人向市政厅投诉。一些奥运选手表示,他们把奖牌视为珍宝,河村咬奖牌是不尊重的、不可接受的行为。

transcript.text: "I would cry if that happened to me," said another athlete, Naohisa Takato. "I handle my own gold medal so gently that I would not scratch it."
transcript.zh: 另一位运动员高藤直寿说:"如果这发生在我身上,我会哭的。我对待自己的金牌非常温柔,不会让它划伤。"

questions.stem: What do the news reports say about the Japanese mayor Takashi Kawamura?

options.text: He apologized for scratching an athlete's gold medal.
He was asked to present a gold medal to Miu Goto.
He bit a softball player's Olympic gold medal.
He attracted public attention at a media event.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：A Japanese mayor apologized Thursday for biting the Olympic gold medal of a softball player.信号：新闻首句即考点 。新闻类录音的第一句往往就是核心事件概述，本题答案直接落在 A Japanese mayor apologized Thursday for biting the Olympic gold medal…

optionAnalysis.A: 张冠李戴：A 项说他为 scratching（刮花）金牌道歉，但录音原文 apologized Thursday for biting 道歉的对象是 bit（咬），不是 scratch。scratch 一词反而出现在第 7 段 I would not scratch it，是另一位运动员说的话，属于张冠李戴。 借用原文：He asked her to put the medal around his neck.
optionAnalysis.B: 与原文相反：B 项说市长被要求把金牌颁给 Miu Goto，但录音 He asked her to put the medal around his neck. 恰恰相反——是市长请运动员把奖牌挂在他自己脖子上，方向颠倒。 借用原文：Nagoya mayor Takashi Kawamura had praised an athlete, Miu Goto, during a public media event.
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：D 项说他在 media event 上吸引了公众关注。录音 during a public media event 确实出现 media event，但'吸引公众关注'是事件附带的结果，不是新闻报道的核心事件，与题干 What do the news reports say about… 的核心不符。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（biting the Olympic gold medal of a softball player ↔ bit a softball player's Olympic gold medal 动名词换过去式）

questions.evidenceText: A Japanese mayor apologized Thursday for biting the Olympic gold medal of a softball player.

questions.stem: What did mayor Takashi Kawamura offer to do?

options.text: Have another picture taken with the Olympic medalist.
Apologize to the International Olympic Committee.
Pay for the cost of a new medal.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：The mayor said the medal was undamaged, though he offered to pay for the cost of a new one.信号：题干原词直接命中 。录音里 he offered to pay for the cost of a new one 直接出现题干的核心动词 offered，紧接其后的 to pay for the cost of a…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：A 项说再拍一张照。录音里确实出现 photographers（第 2 段），但市长并没有提出'再拍一张'，A 是无中生有。
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：B 项说他要向 International Olympic Committee 道歉。录音 Goto, however, has accepted the International Olympic Committee's offer of a replacement 里确实出现 International Olympic Committee，但那是奥委会向运动员提供替换奖牌，与市长的道歉对象无关。市长道歉对象是 reporters（Kawamura told reporters Thursday）。 借用原文：the medal was undamaged
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：C 项预设奖牌已 damaged 需要修，但录音 the medal was undamaged 明确说市长称奖牌并未受损，故无需修复。前缀 un- 一字之差，方向完全相反。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（offered to pay for the cost of a new one ↔ Pay for the cost of a new medal. 代词还原为名词）

questions.evidenceText: The mayor said the medal was undamaged, though he offered to pay for the cost of a new one.

questions.stem: What did some Olympians say they would do with their medals?

options.text: Allow no one to touch them.
See them as symbols of honor.
Keep them in a safe place.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P6）：Some Olympians said they treat their medals as treasures and that it was disrespectful and unacceptable for Kawamura to bite one.信号：题干引述结构对位 。录音 Some Olympians said they treat their medals as treasures 几乎与题干 Some Olympians say they would do…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：A 项说不让任何人碰。录音里没有任何一句话说'不允许任何人触碰'，运动员只是说视若珍宝、会轻拿轻放（I handle my own gold medal so gently），并没有提到 touch 这件事。
optionAnalysis.B: 过度推断：B 项把奖牌看作 symbols of honor（荣誉象征）。录音里运动员说的是 treat as treasures（视若珍宝）和 handle gently（轻拿轻放），并没有上升到'荣誉象征'这种抽象概念，属于过度推断。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：D 项说放在 safe place（安全的地方）。录音通篇没有提到把奖牌放在哪里这一存放地点信息，运动员的表述只关乎'如何对待'与'如何轻拿轻放'，不涉及存放位置。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（they treat their medals as treasures ↔ Treat them as treasures. 近乎原词复现）

questions.evidenceText: Some Olympians said they treat their medals as treasures and that it was disrespectful and unacceptable for Kawamura to bite one.

transcript.text: M: What's that orange thing on your computer screen?
transcript.zh: M: 你电脑屏幕上那个橙色的东西是什么？

transcript.text: W: It's something I bought yesterday. It's a plastic sheet that blocks blue light. I have one that I use to cover my phone screen too.
transcript.zh: W: 这是我昨天买的。是一张能阻挡蓝光的塑料贴膜。我还有一张用来贴手机屏幕的。

transcript.text: M: What do you mean by blue light?
transcript.zh: M: 你说的蓝光是什么意思？

transcript.text: W: Blue light includes natural light, but it also includes light that isn't natural, for example, from computers, phones, televisions and other electronic devices.
transcript.zh: W: 蓝光包括自然光，但也包括非自然光，比如来自电脑、手机、电视和其他电子设备的光。

transcript.text: M: So blue light is harmful and that's why you want to block it.
transcript.zh: M: 所以蓝光是有害的，这就是你想阻挡它的原因。

transcript.text: W: It isn't that simple. Blue light isn't necessarily bad for us. In fact, we need blue light during the day to be healthy. But too much blue light, especially from electronic devices, can harm our health by weakening our vision and making it harder for us to fall asleep. And poor sleep can cause all sorts of health problems.
transcript.zh: W: 没那么简单。蓝光不一定对我们有害。事实上，我们白天需要蓝光来保持健康。但过多的蓝光，尤其是来自电子设备的蓝光，会削弱我们的视力，让我们更难入睡，从而损害我们的健康。而睡眠不好会导致各种健康问题。

transcript.text: M: I'm not so sure that sleep is nearly as important as people always say it is. I haven't slept enough in months because I have too much work to do, and I feel fine. And it's the same for most of my friends. Poor sleep might be a problem for older people, but surely young people can handle late nights.
transcript.zh: M: 我不太确定睡眠真的像人们常说的那么重要。我好几个月都没睡够了，因为工作太多，但我感觉挺好的。我大多数朋友也是这样。睡眠不好可能对老年人是个问题，但年轻人肯定能应付熬夜吧。

transcript.text: W: Well, the research I've read shows that sleep is probably even more important than we thought, and that not having enough sleep can contribute to serious health problems like obesity and heart disease. And all the artificial blue light from electronic devices means we have to try harder to sleep well.
transcript.zh: W: 嗯，我读到的研究表明，睡眠可能比我们想象的还要重要，睡眠不足会导致肥胖和心脏病等严重的健康问题。而且电子设备发出的所有人造蓝光意味着我们必须更努力才能睡好。

transcript.text: M: Maybe you're right. I'm on my computer very late most nights, and that's probably why I don't sleep enough.
transcript.zh: M: 也许你说得对。我大多数晚上都很晚还在用电脑，这可能就是我睡眠不足的原因。

questions.stem: What did the woman do to her computer?

options.text: She covered its screen with a plastic sheet.
She connected it with her smartphone.

transcript.text: W: As a kid, did you know what job you wanted to do when you grew up?

transcript.text: M: No, I didn't. And I got sick every time adults asked me what I wanted to be when I grew up.
transcript.zh: M: 不知道。每次大人问我长大后想做什么，我都觉得烦。

transcript.text: W: It's the same with me. And I'm tired of people asking that question of my 10-year-old daughter. My daughter's stock answers are basketball player, pop singer, mechanical engineer. Adults love that last one, as it's the perfect mix of the sensible and the ambitious. When she was much younger, my daughter used to say she wanted to be Queen of the Clouds, which I loved. That's the kind of goal-setting I like to see in children, springing from their boundless imaginations.
transcript.zh: W: 我也是。我也受够了别人老问我10岁女儿这个问题。我女儿的标准答案是篮球运动员、流行歌手、机械工程师。大人们特别喜欢最后那个，因为它既实际又有抱负，是完美的结合。我女儿小时候曾说她想当云朵女王，我特别喜欢这个。这才是我希望在孩子身上看到的那种目标设定，源于他们无边无际的想象力。

transcript.text: M: Yes, we grown-ups can be tedious and limiting in our need for reality. And we teach a very gloomy image of adulthood—that whatever our children's future holds, it must be seen within the context of a job.
transcript.zh: M: 是啊，我们成年人为了现实可能会变得乏味和局限。而且我们给孩子灌输了一种非常灰暗的成年生活形象——无论我们孩子的未来是什么样的，都必须放在工作这个框架里看。

transcript.text: W: How utterly overwhelming and dull!
transcript.zh: W: 这太让人喘不过气来了，而且多无聊啊！

transcript.text: M: When people ask my son what he wants to be when he grows up, I have to swallow the urge to say, "Hey, back off my kid's dreams!"
transcript.zh: M: 每当有人问我儿子长大后想做什么时，我都得忍住不说：嘿，别对我孩子的梦想指手画脚！

transcript.text: W: We can't dismiss the idea that teenagers have to plan to do something after they finish school, and parents are entitled to hope it's more than simply spending 10 hours a day playing computer games.
transcript.zh: W: 我们不能否认青少年确实需要为毕业后做点什么而规划，家长也有权希望那不仅仅是每天花10个小时玩电脑游戏。

transcript.text: M: But asking "What do you want to be?" isn't going to lead a child to a fulfilled life, rather at least to false expectations and a high chance of disappointment.
transcript.zh: M: 但问"你想做什么"并不会引导孩子走向充实的人生，反而至少会带来错误的期望和很大的失望可能。

transcript.text: W: Exactly. We should be helping our kids understand who they are, even if that means letting go of who we think they should be.
transcript.zh: W: 没错。我们应该帮助孩子了解他们自己是谁，即使这意味着放下我们认为他们应该成为什么样的人。

transcript.text: For years, using recycled plastic to make plastic products was cheap. By contrast, fossil fuel plastic was more expensive. Thus this sustainable option was an economic option too.

transcript.text: But now it is cheaper for major manufacturers to use new plastic.
transcript.zh: 但现在对于大型制造商来说，使用新塑料更便宜。

transcript.text: According to one recent business report, recycled plastic now costs an extra $72 a tonne compared with newly-made plastic. This may be because of consumer demands. They are pushing for more recycled plastics in new products. Meanwhile, new plastic is becoming cheaper. This is because of a boom in petroleum chemical production from the U.S. The price increase of recycled plastic could cost sustainable manufacturers an extra $250 million a year.
transcript.zh: 根据最近的一份商业报告，与新制塑料相比，再生塑料现在每吨要多花费72美元。这可能是因为消费者的需求。他们推动在新产品中使用更多再生塑料。与此同时，新塑料正变得更便宜。这是因为美国石油化工生产的繁荣。再生塑料价格的上涨可能会使可持续制造商每年多支出2.5亿美元。

transcript.text: Smaller manufacturers may also be forced to use new plastic to reduce costs. Makers of clear plastic bottles may also opt for new fossil-fuel based plastic to save money.
transcript.zh: 较小的制造商也可能被迫使用新塑料以降低成本。透明塑料瓶的制造商也可能选择使用新的化石燃料基塑料来省钱。

transcript.text: Plastic packaging makers are being pressured to use more recycled plastic. This is done in hopes of reducing the enormous amount of plastic pollution in the oceans.
transcript.zh: 塑料包装制造商正面临使用更多再生塑料的压力。这样做是为了减少海洋中大量的塑料污染。

transcript.text: The UK government plans to tax companies which don't use at least 30% recycled plastic in their products. Additionally, the government is planning to increase the quantity of recycled plastic in the market.
transcript.zh: 英国政府计划对产品中再生塑料使用量未达到至少30%的公司征税。此外，政府正计划增加市场上再生塑料的数量。

transcript.text: This could mean incentives for new recycling plants. Additionally, recycling facilities may be improved at a local council level and recycled plastic could be imported.
transcript.zh: 这可能意味着对新回收工厂的激励措施。此外，地方议会层面的回收设施可能会得到改善，再生塑料也可以进口。

transcript.text: This would help increase the amount of recycled plastic in circulation.
transcript.zh: 这将有助于增加流通中再生塑料的数量。

transcript.text: At the Dreamery, a business in Manhattan, naps are for sale. A 45-minute session in a darkened enclosure with peace and quiet costs $25. To be clear, this institution is no hotel. This is a nap joint. It sells the idea of the nap as much as the nap itself.
transcript.zh: 在曼哈顿的 Dreamery，小睡是用来出售的。在一个幽暗的封闭空间里享受平静与安宁的 45 分钟小睡需要 25 美元。需要明确的是，这家机构不是酒店。这是一家小睡店。它出售的是小睡这个理念，就像出售小睡本身一样。

transcript.text: Is a nap worth $25? The answer is obviously yes. Here, at this point in the argument, it's traditional for me to bring up all the studies that show the benefits of napping. But do you really need experts to tell you that? Just look at the world around you at 2:30 in the afternoon.
transcript.zh: 一次小睡值 25 美元吗？答案显然是肯定的。在论证的这一点上，按惯例我应该列举所有显示小睡益处的研究。但你真的需要专家告诉你这些吗？只需看看下午两点半你周围的世界。

transcript.text: I've been working from home for more than 10 years now. And the quality and quantity of work I can do emerges directly from my ability to concentrate. I don't understand how people have creative careers without napping. Every day at about 1 p.m., everyone faces the same choice: sleep until 2 p.m. and then work until 5, or daydream and drift around social media and attend pointless meetings until 7 p.m.
transcript.zh: 我在家工作已经超过 10 年了。我能完成的工作质量和数量直接来源于我的专注能力。我不明白人们如何能在不小睡的情况下从事创意职业。每天大约下午一点，每个人都面临同样的选择：睡到下午两点然后工作到五点，或者做白日梦、在社交媒体上闲逛、参加毫无意义的会议直到晚上七点。

transcript.text: The friends I have who still work in offices inform me their bosses insist that they take the second option, and that napping is associated with laziness. I genuinely find it odd. For if you nap properly, it's like waking up from a full night's sleep and you can double your day's worth of concentration.
transcript.zh: 我那些仍在办公室工作的朋友告诉我，他们的老板坚持让他们选择第二种方案，而且小睡被认为与懒惰联系在一起。我真的觉得这很奇怪。因为如果你好好小睡，那就像从一整夜的睡眠中醒来，你可以让一天的专注力翻倍。

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: We're growing more used to chatting to our computers, phones and smart speakers through voice assistants like Amazon's Alexa, Apple's Siri and Microsoft's Cortana. Blind and partially sighted people have been using text-to-speech converters for decades.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Out of these assistants, Siri is the most well-known. The assistant uses voice inquiries and a natural-language user interface(界面) to answer questions. The software adapts to users' individual language usages, searches, and preferences, with continuing use.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Some think voice could soon take over from typing and clicking as the main way to interact online. But what are the challenges of moving to "the spoken web"?

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: What use is written online content if you can't read? That is the situation facing illiterate(不识字的) African farmers. They are often denied crucial information the web offers many others. With a literacy rate in some parts of Africa at only 22.6%, farmers are often "underpaid for their produce because they might be unaware of the prevailing prices," says Francis Dittoh, a researcher behind Mr Meteo, a speech-based weather information service.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: "The most frequently heard complaint is about rainfall predictions," says Mr Dittoh, who lives in Tamale, northern Ghana. "They tell us the methods their forefathers used to predict the weather don't seem to work as well these days." This is down to climate change, he believes. Yet knowing when it's going to rain is vital for farmers wanting to sow seeds, irrigate crops or take their animals out to the fields to feed on grass.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Mr Dittoh says the idea of converting online weather reports into speech came from the farmers themselves, after a workshop in the village of Guabuligah. "They came up with this," he says. Mr Meteo takes the online weather forecast, converts it to a short recording in the appropriate language and makes it available on a basic phone. Farmers ring up to receive the information. The local language Dagbani is spoken by 1.2 million people but is not served by any online translation applications. The service was designed to be cheap and easy to run, says Mr Dittoh. He plans to begin field tests this month, working with Tamale's Savanna Agricultural Research Institute.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The spoken web could also help the one-in-five adults in Europe and the U.S. with poor reading skills. But building the spoken web—web-to-voice and voice-to-web—isn't straightforward. For software to understand that pizza is served at Italian restaurants is easy. To cover multiple domains and to be able to have a conversation with users on every single topic is still a long way off.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: So although many computer assistants can answer simple questions about the weather and play music for us, anything resembling a wide-ranging human conversation is decades away. Artificial intelligence just isn't smart enough yet. Even turning your voice into text—automatic speech recognition—is one of the hardest problems to solve, as there are as many ways to pronounce things as there are people on the planet.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Siri has often been praised for its ability to interpret our casual language and deliver very specific and accurate results, sometimes even providing additional information. But it is still somewhat restricted, particularly when the language moves away from stiffer commands into more human interactions. In one example, the phrase "Send a text to Jason, Clint, Sam, and Lee saying we're having dinner at Silver Cloud restaurant" was interpreted as sending a message to Jason only, containing the text "Clint Sam and Lee saying we're having dinner at Silver Cloud restaurant". It has also been noted that Siri lacks a proper editing function, as saying "Edit message to say: we're at Silver Cloud restaurant and you should come find us" generates "Clint Sam and Lee saying we're having dinner at Silver Cloud restaurant to say we're at Silver Cloud restaurant and you should come find us".

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: Using voice interaction feels far more intimate than surfing the net the old-fashioned way. This is intentional as the informal tone of the assistant helps create an emotional attachment. But if something speaks, it must also listen. Our phones are always near us and they are collecting data about us all the time. This has already raised privacy concerns. The American Civil Liberties Union has stated that digital assistants create a threat to privacy from hackers. Some people have other concerns. They worry assistants will one day be used to deliver advertising directly to us.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: But digital voices need more personality to make them popular. Robots are not yet witty, Siri is boring. The benefits of using voice instead of tapping fingers obviously depend on the context. Doctors completing online forms about their patients by speech, for example, can dictate 150 words a minute, three times faster than typing on a keyboard. This enables them to spend less time on administration and more time with patients.

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: Last year, speech recognition company Nuance helped a doctors' surgery in Dukinfield, near Manchester, set up a speech system for the practice's six doctors. Now they can dictate notes on a patient's health condition and treatment and a smart assistant automatically enters the information into the right fields on a web form. Previously, the doctors made voice recordings that were then transcribed by secretaries—a process that was costly and likely to cause delays. The new system means letters to patients now have more detail.

paragraphs.label: M
paragraphs.text: Using voice also makes sense when you're doing other things with your hands. Think about when you're cooking, and you just want to know what the next step in the recipe is. Your hands are covered with oil; you're not going to get on the iPad, so it's a lot more natural to talk. And speech obviously makes sense when you're driving. In the U.S., 29% of drivers admit they surf behind the wheel, according to insurance firm State Farm. This is up from 13% in 2009. No wonder using mobile phones while driving causes more crashes a year than drink driving, says the U.S. National Safety Council.

Despite this, popular culture and the housing industry market happiness as living with both more space and more amenities(便利设施). Big houses are advertised as a reward for hard work and diligence, turning housing from a basic necessity into a luxury.

paragraphs.label: B

By 2016, the average size of a new, single-family home was 2,422 square feet. What's more, homes built in the 2000s were more likely than earlier models to have more of all types of spaces: bedrooms, bathrooms, living rooms, dining rooms, recreation rooms and garages.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: There are consequences of living big. As middle-class houses have grown larger, two things have happened. First, large houses take time to maintain, so cleaners and other low-wage service workers are required to keep these houses in order. Second, once-public spaces, where people from diverse backgrounds used to come together, have increasingly become privatized, leading to a reduction in the number of public facilities available to all, and a reduced quality of life for many. Take swimming pools. While in 1950, only 2,500 U.S. families owned pools, by 1999 this number was 4 million. At the same time, public municipal pools were often closed, leaving low-income people nowhere to swim.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The trend for bigger housing thus poses ethical questions. Should Americans accept a system in which the middle and upper classes enjoy a luxurious lifestyle, using the low-wage labor of others? Are we willing to accept a system in which an increase in amenities purchased by the affluent means a reduction in amenities for the poor?

paragraphs.label: E

A better goal than building bigger houses for some is to create more publicly accessible spaces and amenities for all.
